preconditions.description: The input integers n, d, and k are within the specified bounds [1, 4*10^5].
The number of vertices n is at least 1.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'NO' if (d >= n or (d > 1 and k == 1)) else (stdout.startswith('YES') and len(stdout.strip().split('\n')) == n and all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()) for line in stdout.strip().split('\n')[1:]))
postconditions.description: If no valid tree exists (d >= n or d > 1 with k=1), output 'NO'. Otherwise, output 'YES' followed by n-1 lines of edges, where each edge connects two valid vertices between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: not (d >= n or (d > 1 and k == 1)) and stdout.startswith('YES') and (lambda edges: (len(edges) == n - 1) and (all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges)) and (len(set(edges)) == len(edges)) and (len({u for u, v in edges} | {v for u, v in edges}) == n) and (all(sum(1 for u, v in edges if u == x or v == x) <= k for x in range(1, n + 1))) and (max(len(path) - 1 for path in [[u for u, v in edges] for u, v in edges]) == d))(stdout.strip().split('\n')[1:]) if not (d >= n or (d > 1 and k == 1)) else True
postconditions.description: If a solution is printed, the edges form a valid tree (n-1 edges, connected, no cycles), every vertex has degree at most k, and the diameter of the tree is exactly d.
